preconditions.description: The input is a list of intervals.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(iv, tuple) and len(iv) == 2 and isinstance(iv[0], int) and isinstance(iv[1], int) for iv in intervals)
preconditions.description: Each element in the list is a tuple of two integers representing an interval.
The number of intervals N is between 1 and 100 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= start <= end <= 1000 for start, end in intervals)
preconditions.description: For every interval [start, end], 0 <= start <= end <= 1000.

postconditions.expression: isinstance(return_value, list) and all(isinstance(iv, tuple) and len(iv) == 2 and isinstance(iv[0], int) and isinstance(iv[1], int) for iv in return_value)
postconditions.description: The output is a list of tuples, each containing two integers.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= start <= end <= 1000 for start, end in return_value)
postconditions.description: Each merged interval in the output satisfies 0 <= start <= end <= 1000.

postconditions.expression: all(return_value[i][0] <= return_value[i+1][0] for i in range(len(return_value)-1))
postconditions.description: The output intervals are sorted by their start times in non-decreasing order.

postconditions.expression: all(return_value[i][1] < return_value[i+1][0] for i in range(len(return_value)-1))
postconditions.description: No two consecutive intervals in the output overlap or touch; they are disjoint.

postconditions.expression: all(any(start <= iv[0] and iv[1] <= end for start, end in intervals) for iv in return_value)
postconditions.description: Every interval in the output is a valid merge of one or more input intervals (i.e., it covers a contiguous range formed by overlapping inputs).

postconditions.expression: all(any(iv[0] <= start and end <= iv[1] for iv in return_value) for start, end in intervals)
postconditions.description: Every input interval is fully contained within exactly one interval in the output.
